title: MAdam: Metric-Aware Multi-Objective Adam
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: Pairing a wrapper with a base optimizer silently breaks the solver's intent, through stale preference weighting and a distorted metric that flips task effects.
layout: 2 panels, side by side; left trajectory contour map, right line plot, bold captions below
description: Two side-by-side panels on a 2D tilted-quadratic toy problem, each titled in bold below. The left panel, Weighting Mismatch, is a contour heatmap with red-to-blue shading, where blue marks low loss. A dashed brown pre-switch path runs from a white 'start' circle to a yellow square marking the switch to λ_B. After the switch, a purple Adam path stalls at a purple dot ('Adam end') near θ*_λA. A yellow MAdam path continues to a yellow dot ('Madam end') next to the red star θ*_λB. The right panel plots signed task effect g_i^T M^-1 d against step, 0 to 500. Black Euclidean curves are the reference, red Adam curves with a shaded region dip negative for task 1, and green MAdam curves track the black reference. The eye goes first to the colorful contour map and the red curve below zero.
caption: Two sources of solver--Adam mismatch on a 2D tilted-quadratic MOO problem. Left (weighting mismatch): decision-space trajectories across a single preference switch $\boldsymbol{\lambda}_A\!\to\!\boldsymbol{\lambda}_B$; contours show the post-switch loss $\ell_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}_B}$ (darker is lower) and the star marks its minimum $\boldsymbol{\theta}^\star_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}_B}$. Adam's second-moment EMA still encodes the pre-switch $\boldsymbol{\lambda}_A$, so its iterate stalls near $\boldsymbol{\theta}^\star_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}_A}$, while \method{} re-conditions to the active preference and reaches $\boldsymbol{\theta}^\star_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}_B}$ (Prop. [ref]; multi-phase version in App. [ref]). Right (geometric mismatch): per-objective signed effect $g_i^{\!\top}M^{-1}d$ on the same problem. Under the Euclidean metric ($M=I$) it is non-negative for every task, so any negative value is a sign flip against the solver's intent. Adam's preconditioner drives task 1 strongly negative (shaded), so the update increases $\ell_1$ although the solver treats task 1 as aligned with $d$; \method{} tracks the Euclidean reference and largely removes the flip (Prop. [ref]; mechanism in App. [ref]).
abstract: Multi-objective optimization (MOO) underlies many machine learning problems, yet MOO solvers across the loss-balancing, gradient-balancing, and Pareto-based families almost universally hand their reconciled directions to Adam~\citep{kingma2015adam}. We show this coupling introduces two systematic gaps between the solver's intent and the optimizer's execution. The first is a weighting mismatch: Adam's second-moment denominator entangles the time-varying preference vector with gradient statistics, marginalizing the preference into a history average and collapsing distinct Pareto trade-offs toward a near-uniform mixture. The second is a geometric mismatch: Adam's adaptive metric distorts the Euclidean geometry MOO solvers assume, turning aligned objectives into apparent conflicts. To resolve both jointly, we introduce MAdam (Metric-Aware Multi-Objective Adam), a drop-in wrapper that leaves both solver and optimizer unchanged. MAdam preconditions the reconciled direction by the preference-conditioned curvature of the scalarized objective; on this whitened input, Adam's second moment collapses to identity, so the realized update is governed by the preference-conditioned metric. Across multi-task learning, Pareto-front recovery, physics-informed neural networks, and medical imaging, MAdam improves over Adam in aggregate for every solver family. Our code is available at https://github.com/lfb-1/MAdam.
